newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy renounces use of anti-personnel mines.
newsitem.headline: Italy renounces use of anti-personnel mines.

text.p: Italy renounced the use of anti-personnel mines on Friday, saying the move was aimed at helping to reach an international agreement on their use.
A statement from the office of Prime Minister Romano Prodi said the cabinet had agreed earlier on Friday to end the "operational use" of mines.
The step followed measures already taken to stop production and export of mines and to start destroying them.
The decision had been taken "to contribute to reaching a solid international agreement and a definitive solution to the problem posed by anti-personnel mines," the statement said.
The United States and other Western nations are pushing for talks on a global ban on landmines which are blamed for killing 25,000 people a year and maiming more, mainly civilians.

A 61-member Conference on Disarmament, backed by the United Nations, has been trying in Geneva this week to start discussions. Progress has been blocked by Mexico, which says it does not regard the Geneva forum as appropriate for the talks.
